data.narrative:
Newspace Research, a Series B defense and security company that has raised $73.2M to date, is valued against a universe of 10 comparable companies—2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms including Dream Security, Harmattan AI, Code Metal, Castelion, and Defense Unicorns.

Two valuation methods triangulate the company's worth. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $73M raised proxy, implying $139M. Peer-median valuation examines 7 same-sector, same-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.0B and a range spanning $300M to $3.0B, directly implying $1.0B. The peer distribution reflects material variance: Dream Security trades at $3.0B while lower-quartile peers cluster around $1.0B–$1.2B.

The triangulated analysis yields a low of $118M, median of $570M, and high of $1.1B. The wide dispersion—spanning nearly one order of magnitude—reflects structural uncertainty in defense-tech valuation at this stage. Key risks include capital intensity of the business model, customer concentration (often government), and technology differentiation relative to the peer set. The peer-median method carries greater weight given the sample size and sector specificity, but the stage-progression anchor remains conservative and appropriate absent revenue data or proprietary technology multipliers in the record.
